items.headline: Nasdaq sinks 2.1% Friday and posts its worst week since June
items.note: The S&P 500 fell 1.1% to 7,659.44 and the Dow slipped 0.3% to 52,002.41, but the Dow still rose 0.7% on the week while the Nasdaq lost about 4.5%. Selling in chip and software stocks and a jump in oil prices drove it.

items.headline: CoreWeave falls again on worries about its heavy debt
items.note: The AI data-center company is under pressure over its debt-heavy balance sheet, and a BofA analyst called the selling "more sentiment driven" than about fundamentals. It shows how AI-buildout financing is now what moves the stocks of the companies you may want to work for.

items.headline: Oil hits $110 a barrel and Treasury yields stay high
items.note: Brent touched $110 for the first time since May as Iran escalated attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, and the 10-year yield was near 5.1%. Futures still point to roughly one more Fed quarter-point hike by December.

items.headline: Google opens Gemini 4 Argon to developers and consumers
items.note: Its latest frontier model is now in AI Studio, the Gemini app and Search AI Mode, with API pricing of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens during a promotional period. Good one to try for projects.

items.headline: ASML reports record quarterly revenue
items.note: Third-quarter sales were €11.7 billion with €5 billion net income, and customers are already discussing equipment needs for 2029 and 2030. Chip demand looks strong even as chip stocks fall.

items.headline: Japan to fund two GlobalFoundries chip factories in New York
items.note: Japan will invest up to $21 billion in two New York state semiconductor plants, part of a larger U.S.-Japan investment deal. It could mean more chip jobs in the region.

learn.explain: Volatility is how much and how fast prices swing up and down. The VIX is a number, often called the market's fear gauge, that estimates how much traders expect the S&P 500 to swing over the next 30 days, based on prices of options on the index. A reading around 12-15 means calm, and the VIX rises when investors get nervous. Today's example: after Friday's tech sell-off the VIX rose to roughly 20, a sign traders are bracing for bigger swings.
